chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him (peace be upon him) said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should not buy silver with gold except hand-to-hand, nor buy gold with silver except hand-to-hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for exchanging gold for silver in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith traces the ruling on gold-for-silver exchange back to Imam al-Sadiq and ultimately to Imam Ali, establishing the 'hand-to-hand' (yadan bi yadin) requirement to prevent riba al-fadl. This principle ensures immediate physical possession and equal weight, serving as a foundational safeguard against usury in Islamic commercial jurisprudence. It highlights the continuity of prophetic tradition in maintaining economic justice through precise transactional rules.
